title: Service Lifecycle Orchestration Guidelines
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This guideline defines a standardized, automated, and auditable lifecycle for platform services at Redwood Inference — from initial onboarding through operational maturity to deprecation and retirement. The goal is predictable reliability, consistent observability, and low cognitive load for on-call and platform teams.

Scope: Applies to any service running on Redwood platform (hosted control plane, edge routing proxies, model-serving adapters, autoscaler, monitoring exporters). This does not replace product-level contractual deprecation notices to customers but aligns internal platform processes with customer-facing timelines.

Owners and Accountability

- Platform team (eng-platform) is the process owner for lifecycle orchestration.
- Service owner: every service must declare a primary and secondary owner in the service catalog. Owners are responsible for onboarding artifacts, SLOs, and retirement plan.
- SRE: responsible for runbook verification, alert thresholds, and incident readiness checks.

Quick summary of phases

1. Proposal & Design (Pre-onboarding)
2. Onboarding & Baseline (Day 0–30)
3. Operational Maturity (30–90 days)
4. Long-term Maintenance (90+ days)
5. Deprecation & Retirement

Required artifacts before onboarding (table)

| Artifact | Required | Example / Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Service README | yes | Ownership, purpose, contact info, SLA class |
| Git repo + CI | yes | Branch protection, linting, automated tests |
| Deployment manifest | yes | Helm/Kustomize chart or Terraform module |
| SLO / Error budget | yes | Availability (%) and latency P95 goals |
| Observability dashboard | yes | Grafana dashboard ID, instrumentation guide |
| Runbook | yes | Incident playbook and escalation steps |
| Security review | conditional | Required for data-sensitive services |

Onboarding checklist (detailed)

- Preflight (owner): create service card in Service Catalog with description, owners, and repo link.
- Template: instantiate onboarding template at platforms/templates/service-starter. Use `make platform-onboard SERVICE=my-service` to populate defaults.
- CI/CD: ensure pipeline has deploy, smoke-test, and canary stages. Required steps: unit tests -> integration tests -> canary deploy (5% traffic) -> automated rollback on >=5% error increase.
- Observability: add metrics (prometheus): `service_requests_total`, `service_request_duration_seconds` (histogram), `service_errors_total`.
- Dashboards: import dashboard template id: PLT-SVC-BASE and wire to service_labels. Add panels for request rate, p95 latency, error rate, instance CPU/GPU usage.
- Logs: structured JSON logging, request_id present. Forward to central Loki/Elasticsearch with retention policy aligned to the SLA class.
- Security: complete the lightweight security checklist (see section Security and Compliance).
- Final review: SRE signs off on runbook and alert thresholds. Onboarding approval recorded in service card.

Operational readiness gates (automated checks)

- CI green with required checks present.
- Dashboard panels have data for 24 hours.
- Error budget defined and > 99.9% availability target set for production services unless otherwise approved.
- Canary rollback automation present.
- API contract tests pass against stubbed clients.

Sample SLO table (as a template)

| SLO Name | Target | Measurement window | Alert threshold | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Availability | 99.9% | 28d | <= 99.7% triggers P1 | service-owner@example.com |
| Request latency P95 | 250ms | 7d | >300ms for 4h triggers P2 | service-owner@example.com |
| Error rate | 0.5% | 1d | >1.0% for 30m triggers P1 | service-owner@example.com |

Dashboard & alert templates

Use the platform-managed Grafana folder `PLATFORM/SERVICES` and import the `PLT-SVC-BASE` dashboard as a baseline. The default alert rules are deployed via the platform alert manager config. Key alert families:

- Latency regressions: p95 > target for 1h -> P2, sustained 4h -> P1.
- Error spikes: rolling 5m error rate > 5x baseline -> immediate P1.
- Capacity saturation: GPU/utilization > 85% on >50% of instances -> P2.
- Missing telemetry: no metrics emitted for 10m -> P1.

Escalation policy (summary)

1. PagerDuty primary on-call for the service (duration: 30m).
2. If unresolved, page platform SRE rotation.
3. After 60m, involve engineering manager and platform lead.
4. For customer-impacting incidents, notify customer-success within 30m.

Runbook template (included in repo as RUNBOOK.md)

- Impact assessment: Is traffic degraded or complete outage? Record time & customer impact.
- Quick mitigation: toggle feature-flag or scale down problematic nodes.
- Reproduce locally with load test harness: `tools/loadtest --target https://staging.my-service`
- Restore from backup (if applicable) — follow data restore SOP.
- Root cause analysis (RCA): start within 24 hours, publish within 72 hours.

Canary and rollout patterns

- Default canary window: 15–30 minutes at 5–10% traffic, then 50% for 1 hour, then full.
- Automated rollback triggers: error rate increase >=3x baseline OR latency p95 > 2x target for 10m.
- Traffic shaping: use platform traffic router (route-manager) with `canaryWeight` parameter. Example YAML snippet: 

```
apiVersion: route.redwood/v1
kind: TrafficPolicy
metadata:
  name: my-service-canary
spec:
  canary:
    weight: 5
    duration: 15m
  steps:
    - weight: 50
      duration: 60m
    - weight: 100
```

Deprecation & retirement policy

- Announcement cadence: 90 days notice for internal-only services, 180 days for customer-facing APIs.
- Required artifacts before retirement: migration plan, dependent services list, archive snapshot, and final RCA if retiring due to defect.
- Final deletion: at least 30 days after marking retired in the catalog. Backup retention policy must be documented.

Automation hooks (APIs and CLI)

- Service Catalog API endpoints (examples):
  - POST /catalog/services -> create card
  - PATCH /catalog/services/:id -> update owners/SLOs/status
  - POST /catalog/services/:id/onboard -> trigger onboarding workflow

- CLI examples: `rwcatalog create --name my-service --owner maya@redwood.ai --slo availability=99.9`

Health-check gating for deploys

Deploy pipeline must run a health-check stage that validates:
- `/healthz` returns 200 from at least 3 AZs
- p95 latency calculated from synthetic traffic within 20% of expected
- no new errors in logs with level >= ERROR

Operational retrospectives (required cadence)

- Post-onboarding retrospective at 30 days to review telemetry, paging noise, and runbook gaps.
- Quarterly health review for each service with owners and SRE to revalidate SLOs and costs.
- After every P1 incident, an RCA and action items must be created with owners and deadlines.

Security and compliance checks

- Data classification: mark whether the service handles sensitive PII or model training inputs.
- KMS integration required for services persisting secrets.
- Penetration test required for externally-facing services before GA.

Appendices

1) Onboarding automation checklist (CLI commands):
- `make platform-onboard SERVICE=my-service`
- `rwcatalog create --name my-service --owner maya@redwood.ai`
- `helm upgrade --install my-service ./charts/my-service --namespace prod`

2) Example ownership change PR description:
- Title: `service(my-service): change primary owner to @new-owner`
- Body: list current owners, reason, phone and pager info, and runbook link.

3) Template links:
- Service starter repo: platforms/templates/service-starter
- Dashboard baseline: Grafana folder `PLATFORM/SERVICES` -> `PLT-SVC-BASE`
- Runbook template: platforms/templates/RUNBOOK.md

Contact and feedback

- Platform lifecycle owner: eng-platform@redwood.ai (Maya Patel)
- Slack channel: #eng-platform-lifecycle for quick questions and rollout notices.

Change log

- 2025-08-12: Initial draft and rollout of onboarding templates.
- 2025-11-03: Added canary automation examples and alert families.
- 2026-02-18: Clarified SLO templates and shortened onboarding window for small infra services.
